reviews.title: Not for a Beginners
reviews.text:
This app does have some nice integrations in the Apple ecosystem but it’s is not for beginners. Their beginner courses have poor directions fast timing and will move to a position and pace not realistic for beginners. They do not offer modified positions. 

Every course I watched gave off the feel of someone who does not understand body mechanics of overweight and obese.

I’m sure this app is great for intermediate and advanced users.

reviews.title: No options for perimenopause, menopausal nor post menopause women
reviews.text:
Nike Training Club is missing an important opportunity to support women in perimenopause, menopause, and post-menopause.

There should be programs specifically designed for this stage of life, with a focus on strength, muscle and bone health, mobility, cardiovascular fitness, weight management, and recovery.

Women do not stop being athletes as we age. Nike should lead by creating fitness programs that recognize and support women through every stage of life.

reviews.title: Awful
reviews.text: I have been using the app for so many years and loved it but over the last few years the app has become difficult. It logs me out, tells me I can’t access things but takes me back to the same place. I’ve become increasingly frustrated with it and saddened by constantly renegotiating how I interact with the app.

reviews.title: Did Kevin in accounts vibe code this?
reviews.text:
The excercises are good but the interface looks like a part time project for. Well done Kevin! But in comparison to other fitness apps this is very poor.  No voice over for excercises. No guide on form. No timing during the workout. 
Professional filmed fitness coach but it’s not clear when it loads or not. And you can’t move the screen from one section to another. Can’t connect music to the progress. Etc. 
Please Nike, buy or copy apps like Sworkit or like any yoga app.
